title: Mainaka
hook: halfway across the sea, a golden mountain rises out of the water and offers Hanuman a place to rest

segments.voice: Yesterday: the leap, the long flight, trees falling behind Hanuman like family at the gate. Did you message someone who once saw you off? Today, someone in the middle of the sea wants to help. Day six hundred six.

You're driving a long way, late, and a friend texts: you're passing my town, come in, I've made dinner, sleep here tonight. It's a real kindness. And you know that if you stop, you won't get where you're going in time. That's the first test Hanuman meets over the ocean, and it isn't a monster. It's a gift. The sea itself has been watching him, and the sea feels it owes him something.
screen: `COME IN, I'VE MADE DINNER.` → `THE FIRST TEST IS A GIFT.`

segments.voice: In Valmiki's telling, the Ocean is a person who thinks and remembers. And the Ocean remembers a debt. Long ago, King Sagara, an ancestor of Rama's own family line, had sons who dug out the bed of the sea. That's why one of the Ocean's names is sagara. So the Ocean thinks: this monkey is on an errand for Rama, a son of the family that made me what I am. I should help him. He shouldn't wear himself out. So the Ocean calls to a mountain hidden beneath its waves, Mainaka, and asks him to rise up and give the traveler a place to rest. Mainaka lifts out of the water, golden peaks shining, trees on his slopes, and takes a human form on the summit, and invites Hanuman to stop, rest, eat fruit, and then go on. Hanuman's first reaction, Valmiki says, is suspicion: a mountain suddenly rising in his path looks like an obstacle, and he pushes it aside with his chest. Then Mainaka explains, and Hanuman understands. He answers with great courtesy. I'm grateful, he says. Your welcome is as good as done. But time is pressing, and I've promised not to stop on the way. And he touches the mountain with his hand, a touch that honors the offer, and flies on. This is the quietest kind of test. Refusing a threat is easy to understand. Refusing kindness without hurting the person offering it takes skill. Hanuman doesn't lecture Mainaka. He doesn't rest a little to be polite. He receives the gift by touching it, and keeps his promise.
screen: `THE OCEAN REMEMBERS A DEBT.` · `MAINAKA RISES TO OFFER REST.` · `TIME PRESSES; I'VE PROMISED.` · then, large: `HE TOUCHES THE MOUNTAIN AND GOES ON.`

segments.voice: Sit and breathe. Rest one hand lightly on your knee or the arm of your chair, the way Hanuman's hand touches the mountain. Think of an offer you'll probably have to turn down soon: an invitation, a favor, a kind distraction. Breathe in, and feel grateful for it, genuinely. Breathe out, and keep your direction. Let the hand stay light, honoring without holding. The bell holds the time.
Mainaka. The golden mountain under the sea who rises, at the Ocean's request, to offer Hanuman rest, and whom Hanuman thanks with a touch of his hand before flying on.
Your line: Mainaka. Today, if you turn down a kind offer, thank the person warmly first, and keep going. Day six hundred six.

howItsDone: In Sundara Kanda recitations, Mainaka is remembered as the first of three meetings over the sea, and Hanuman's touch of the mountain is often explained as accepting the hospitality without stopping.

options: rest for a night; you've earned it.
thank him, touch the mountain, and fly on.

original.note: Sanskrit maināka, the mountain in the sea.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hanuman's tests over the sea are all monsters.
what it means: the first one is a gift, and the test is declining it gracefully.
what a scholar hears: the Ocean's gratitude ties this scene to the Bala Kanda story of King Sagara's sons, linking Hanuman's crossing to Rama's ancestry.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 1 (the Ocean's request; Mainaka rises; Hanuman declines)

notes: The Ocean's reasoning (debt to the Ikshvaku line through Sagara's sons) and Mainaka's human form on the summit: confirm against Sundara 1.
Hanuman first pushes Mainaka aside with his chest as an obstacle, then understands: confirm.
Bala Kanda sarga range for the Sagara story: confirm.
The explanation of the name sagara for the ocean is traditional; confirm the Keeper is comfortable with it.
